newsitem.title: USA: Nord sets Ontario gold mining venture.
newsitem.headline: Nord sets Ontario gold mining venture.

text.p: Nord Pacific Ltd said Wednesday it has agreed in principle with Young-Shannon Gold Mines Ltd to invest in certain gold mining properties in Chester Township, Ontario.
Under the terms of the proposed agreement, Nord Pacific said, it will have the right to earn a 65 percent interest in the properties by spending C$4,875,000 within 42 months.
Nord Pacific will manage the project and is currently conducting legal and technical due diligence, as well as working with Young-Shannon on a project path and schedule.
Young-Shannon drilling between 1987 and 1991 identified resources of 1,077,907 tons at 0.20 ounces of gold per ton, on what is known as the "C" Gold Zone, Nord said.

A high grade zone, known as the "C-Prime" Gold Zone, showed drill-indicated potential of 695,787 tons at 0.344 ounces of gold per ton. The "C" Gold Zone is open for expansion at depth and along strike.
Nord said additional exploration is planned to test extensions at depth of the "C-Prime" Gold Zone, and to explore newly discovered zones on the properties.

"If sufficient reserves can be developed, this project offers the attractive possibility of early production in an important Canadian gold producing province with well developed infrastructure," Nord said.

The properties lie within the Swayze Greenstone Belt, on assemblage of east-west striking, steeply dipping Archean felsic and mafic flows, pyroclastics and metasediments. This belt may be the western extension of the Abitibi Superbelt, host for important base and precious metal deposits from Chibougamau through Val d'Or, Kirkland Lake, and Timmins.
